_README: Organisations that may be able to help Harry with money, training or
placement. Three groups, all of which he plausibly qualifies for:
VETERAN     He served in the Royal Navy 2021-2023. Two years is under
the four-year mark, which makes him an EARLY SERVICE LEAVER -
a specific category with its own provision, not a lesser one.
YOUNG       He is 22. Most youth funds run to 25 or 30.
LOCAL       Aberdeen and Scotland have their own employability money.
WHAT HE ACTUALLY NEEDS, IN ORDER
1. OPITO BOSIET + MIST offshore survival tickets. Around GBP 1,000-1,300,
and effectively mandatory for offshore work - which is the market his
trade sits in and the one the job machine now searches. This single
item is the difference between being able to apply offshore and not.
2. A driving licence. The scorer flags 'does not drive' as his one real
constraint on where he can work.
3. Anything toward finishing the BEng he paused, or short electrical /
instrumentation tickets (CompEx, 17th/18th Edition, PAT, IPAF).
HONESTY RULES - THESE ARE CHARITIES
- The email ASKS whether he is eligible. It never asserts that he is,
never claims hardship he has not described, and never implies an
entitlement. If an entry in this file is wrong, the worst that happens
is somebody replies 'not us, sorry'.
- No address is ever guessed. The name and website here are the input;
the pipeline's ordinary discovery finds a real, MX-checked address or
sends nothing at all.
- One approach per organisation, ever.
VERIFY BEFORE TRUSTING
This list was written from knowledge, not from a live check of each
organisation's current criteria - web research was unavailable when it
was built. Names and domains are the parts most likely to be stale.
Anything marked "confidence": "check" is one I am less sure of.

organisations.name: Forces Employment Charity
organisations.note: Harry has signed up. Left here so nothing writes to them again.

organisations.name: Career Transition Partnership Future Horizons
organisations.ask: Future Horizons is the CTP programme specifically for Early Service Leavers - under four years' service, which is him. Ask what it can fund and whether he is still in scope three years on.

organisations.name: Royal Navy and Royal Marines Charity
organisations.ask: Grants to RN veterans. Ask specifically about funding OPITO offshore survival tickets and a driving licence.

organisations.name: Poppyscotland
organisations.ask: Scotland's veteran charity, employment and training support. Ask about training grants for a Scottish veteran going into the energy sector.

organisations.name: SSAFA the Armed Forces Charity
organisations.ask: Casework and welfare grants. Ask what their Aberdeen branch can help a young veteran with toward employment costs.

organisations.name: Royal British Legion
organisations.ask: Grants including toward training and equipment for work.

organisations.name: Legion Scotland
organisations.ask: Scottish veterans' support and local branches in the north east.

organisations.name: Veterans Scotland
organisations.ask: Umbrella body - ask which of their member organisations funds training for a young veteran in Aberdeen.

organisations.name: The Seafarers Charity
organisations.ask: Maritime-specific. His Royal Navy service and his subsea work both sit in their world.

organisations.name: Help for Heroes
organisations.ask: Career recovery support. Ask whether their programmes are open to a veteran without a service injury.

organisations.name: The King's Trust
organisations.ask: Development Awards fund tools, course fees, licences and travel for 16-30s. This is the most likely single source of the OPITO tickets or a driving licence.

organisations.name: Skills Development Scotland
organisations.ask: Individual Training Accounts and other funded training for someone out of work in Scotland.

organisations.name: Aberdeen City Council employability
organisations.ask: No One Left Behind employability funding, and what the council offers a young Aberdeen resident going into the energy sector.

organisations.name: North East Scotland College
organisations.ask: Part-time and funded engineering courses, and whether his paused BEng year counts toward anything.

organisations.name: ECITB
organisations.ask: The engineering construction industry's training board - scholarships and funded training routes into the sector.

organisations.name: OPITO
organisations.ask: They set the offshore survival standard. Ask whether any funded or subsidised route to BOSIET and MIST exists for a veteran entering the industry.

organisations.name: Energy Transition Zone
organisations.ask: Aberdeen's energy transition skills body - training and placement programmes.

organisations.name: Lowland Reserve Forces and Cadets Association
organisations.note: Runs the Defence Employer Recognition Scheme across the Scottish Lowlands and announces the award winners. They hold the list of employers who have committed to supporting the armed forces community, and brokering between those employers and service leavers is what the organisation is for.

organisations.name: Highland Reserve Forces and Cadets Association
organisations.note: The same for the Highlands and the north east, which is Harry's own area. Covers Aberdeen, Aberdeenshire and Moray.

organisations.name: Defence Relationship Management
organisations.note: The MoD team that runs the Covenant and the Employer Recognition Scheme nationally. Left here as a record: a central government mailbox is the wrong door for one person's job search, and the RFCAs above are the same route with a regional desk that answers.

organisations.name: Veterans Employment Transition Support
organisations.note: Matches service leavers to employers who have committed to hiring them, which is the guaranteed-interview end of the market rather than the training-funding end.
